title: Lunar eclipse
summary: From bright Moon to red 'blood Moon' and back.

media.alt: Sequence of the Moon moving out of Earth's shadow

blocks.text: A lunar eclipse is **safe to look at** with your eyes, binoculars and the camera. No filter needed.

steps: Check the date and your local times at timeanddate.com (search 'lunar eclipse'). Totality can last over an hour.
Find a spot with a clear view of where the Moon will be. Cloud is the main enemy, so check the forecast.
Set up exactly as for an ordinary Moon: telephoto, tripod, manual focus on the Moon's edge.
During the partial phase expose for the **bright part**. The shadowed part will look black at first.
As totality nears, the Moon dims a lot. Lengthen the shutter, then raise ISO. Bracket to be safe.
In totality, keep the shutter under about 2 s at 300 mm or the Moon smears as it moves.

items: Shoot every 5 minutes from the same spot to build a sequence later.
A wide shot with the red Moon over a landscape works well at a shorter focal length and 4–8 s.
